summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Seed adaptations: Dormancy & perennation. Dispersal strategies: Anemochory (wind: winged Pinus/Cinchona, pappus), Hydrochory (water: fibrous coconut mesocarp), Zoochory (animals: hooks Xanthium, fleshy fruits), Autochory (explosive turgor propulsion Impatiens).

conceptBreakdown.content:
Seeds represent the pinnacle of land plant evolutionary adaptation, decoupling reproduction from liquid water dependencies and enabling long-distance colonization.

### 10.1 Evolutionary Significance of the Seed
1. **Dormancy & Perennation**: Embryo metabolic activity slows to baseline, protected by dehydration ($10\text{--}15\%$ moisture) and a tough seed coat, allowing plants to bridge harsh winter freezes or severe droughts.
2. **Nutritional Provisioning**: Maternal endosperm or cotyledon reserves nourish the young seedling until its photosynthetic leaves emerge.

### 10.2 Dispersal Syndromes (Chory)

| Dispersal Syndrome | Environmental Vector | Morphological Adaptations | Exemplar Species |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Anemochory** | Wind / Air currents | Winged seeds, persistent feathery pappus calyx, parachute hairs, ciliate plumes | *Cinchona, Pinus, Acer* (Samara), *Taraxacum* (Dandelion), *Calotropis* |
| **Hydrochory** | Water currents / Streams | Buoyant pericarp, air-filled intercellular spaces, fibrous water-resistant mesocarp | *Cocos nucifera* (Coconut), *Nymphaea* (Water Lily), *Nelumbo* (Lotus) |
| **Zoochory** | Animals / Birds | Hooked spines, adhesive barbs, viscous mucilage, brightly colored edible fleshy pericarp | *Xanthium* (Cocklebur), *Martynia, Boerhavia, Ficus, Guava* |
| **Autochory** | Explosive Turgor / Ballistics | Sudden release of hydrostatic turgor pressure or hygroscopic mechanical twisting | *Impatiens* (Touch-me-not), *Ecballium elaterium* (Squirting cucumber), *Oxalis* |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Lupinus Arctic Seed Viability Record
conceptBreakdown.title: Lupinus Arctic Seed Viability Record
conceptBreakdown.content: Viable seeds of Arctic Tundra Lupine (Lupinus arcticus) excavated from frozen permafrost germinated and flowered after approximately 10,000 years of dormancy.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Phoenix dactylifera King Herod Record
conceptBreakdown.title: Phoenix dactylifera King Herod Record
conceptBreakdown.content: A date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) seed excavated from King Herod's palace near the Dead Sea successfully germinated after over 2,000 years of dormancy.
